Goobers v0.6.0 enables generated child workflows on the Temporal engine by
default after real-backend, failover, custody, and Kubernetes qualification.

## Highlights

- Enable `task.childWorkflows` for new engine runs by default. The v1 protocol
  supports wait/discard only; merge and replace remain unavailable.
- Preserve rollback through `engine.childWorkflows.enabled: false`. The posture
  is pinned per run, so in-flight runs keep the setting with which they started.
- Fail closed after child-capable pod custody: an ambiguous pod error ends the
  run with `childHandoffFailure` instead of re-dispatching the parent stage after
  a child may already have been admitted.

## Accepted child-workflow residual risks

| ID | Residual risk | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Shared-key grant mint | Control refuses unbound grants. |
| R2 | Failover over-admit | At most one extra admission per parent. |
| R3 | Retired receipts | Retained 30 days after the parent settles; older continuations fail with `ErrResultRetired`. |
| R4 | Child bearer | Present in the pod environment and scoped to the attempt. |
| R5 | Worker keep-alive | Bounded by grant TTL and the Temporal `RUNNING` check. |
| R6 | Strict policy freeze | May cause spurious drift refusals, never unsafe admission. |
| R7 | No merge/replace | v1 supports wait/discard only. |

## Upgrade note

Cloud schemas from any v0.6.0 alpha require a stop-the-world upgrade to v0.6.0
stable. Stop every alpha pod before migration, take a restorable backup, and do
not restart alpha binaries against the upgraded database. See
[`docs/guides/cloud-operations.md`](../../docs/guides/cloud-operations.md) for
the complete upgrade and rollback procedure.
